lecons.title: Plural of nouns ending in f or fe
lecons.summary: Most nouns that end in f or fe change that ending to ves when they mean more than one: knife becomes knives. But a small group keeps the f and only adds s: chief becomes chiefs, never chieves. Learn the rule, then learn the group that escapes it.

notions.statement: A noun ending in f or fe usually changes that ending to ves when it means more than one.

explanations.body: You take away the f or the fe at the end, and you put ves instead.
Like changing shoes at the door: the foot is the same, only what is at the end changes.

lecons.title: Nouns with a special plural
lecons.summary: Some nouns do not take s at all. Their letters change inside the word: foot becomes feet, mouse becomes mice, child becomes children. A few do not change at all: one sheep, many sheep. These words are learnt one by one, like faces.
lecons.illustration_prompt: Figure composée, non générée, dessinée par work/figures-klein-anglais-nov.py. Le mot foot à gauche, une flèche, le mot feet à droite.

notions.statement: In some nouns the two letters oo become ee: foot becomes feet, tooth becomes teeth, goose becomes geese.
notions.illustration_prompt: Figure composée, non générée, dessinée par work/figures-klein-anglais-nov.py. Trois lignes : foot/feet, tooth/teeth, goose/geese.

explanations.body: No s is added at all. The change happens inside the word.
The two round letters oo open up and become two straight ones, ee.

lecons.title: Jumbled letters
lecons.summary: Jumbled letters are the letters of one word, mixed up. Every letter is there and none is missing: your work is to put them back in order so that the word means something. Find the vowels first, then try a beginning, then read it to check.
lecons.illustration_prompt: Figure composée, non générée, dessinée par work/figures-klein-anglais-nov.py. Les lettres s c o o h l en désordre en haut, et school remis en ordre en dessous.

explanations.body: Every letter you need is already there. Not one more, not one less.

lecons.title: The magic e
lecons.summary: A silent e at the end of a word changes the vowel before it: cap becomes cape, hat becomes hate, kit becomes kite. The e itself is never said. And the same sound can sometimes be written another way, with ai or ay, which is where mistakes happen.
lecons.illustration_prompt: Figure composée, non générée, dessinée par work/figures-klein-anglais-nov.py. Le mot cap à gauche, une flèche, le mot cape à droite avec le e en couleur.

notions.statement: When a silent e is added at the end, the vowel before it says its own name: cap becomes cape.
notions.illustration_prompt: Figure composée, non générée, dessinée par work/figures-klein-anglais-nov.py. Trois paires : cap/cape, hat/hate, kit/kite, avec le e ajouté en couleur.

explanations.body: The e at the end wakes up the vowel in the middle and makes it say its letter name.
The e is like a torch at the back of the word: it does not make a sound, it lights up the vowel in front of it.
